DoubleFloats Accuracy Report

Generated by docs/reports/accuracies.jl on Julia 1.13.3.

This report samples a representative subset; it does not cover all available functions.

Double64

Scalar errors are measured against a 512-bit BigFloat reference. For nonzero references, the tables divide relative error by the working precision unit, 1 ulp = 2⁻¹⁰⁴ (about 4.9e-32) relative. Each worst value is the maximum over the listed samples.

Exponentials and Logarithms

functiondomainsamplesmedian (ulps)worst (ulps)
exp(-100, 100) ordinary range2500.090.72
expm1(-1, 1)2500.070.93
exp2(-100, 100) ordinary range2500.080.52
log(0, 100)2500.060.42
log1 ± 2⁻³¹2500.040.56
log1p(-1, 1)2500.050.38
log2(0, 100)2500.040.42

Exponential rounding near the format limits

For exp and exp2, the main table reports relative working-precision units for finite results with reference at or above Δ / eps(Double64). Here Δ is the smallest positive subnormal of the underlying float. The subnormal range lies below the underlying float's minimum normal. The quantization-limited normal range lies between that minimum and Δ / eps(Double64).

The lattice tables compare the sum of the two returned components with the nearest multiple of Δ in these two ranges. They also show absolute error and error measured in steps of Δ. Output outcome counts describe the returned values and can overlap the reference range counts. A zero or overflow disagreement compares the outcome with round-to-nearest thresholds for the underlying format. Targeted probes use 1536-bit references to resolve low components as small as the underlying subnormal spacing.

Matrix Functions (identity residuals)

The matrix rows measure how closely the results satisfy the listed identities on random matrices. Each residual uses the largest entry magnitude, divided by dimension and working epsilon. The logarithm and square root rows also divide by the largest input entry magnitude. An unavailable row indicates an error during that measurement.

Double32 vector kernels

These rows use dense, disjoint vectors passed to DoubleFloats.simdmap!. The inputs are sampled by high word, with a low word of magnitude 2^-90 on every eighth element. The comparison includes both words of each input in the 512-bit reference. The Technical Guide describes the scalar and batch ranges.
